name: logos-marquee

frames.best_why: Frame 2 shows six logo marks at near-full brightness, with Apple and Google clearly centred.

tagline: Brand logos glide sideways on a dark strip and fade at both ends.
summary: A single row of well-known company logos drifts sideways on a dark rounded panel and loops endlessly. Soft fades at each end hide the cut edges so the row appears to run on without a join.
appearance: A dark charcoal rounded panel holds one evenly spaced row of white and grey logo marks — Facebook, OpenAI, X, Apple and Google repeating — on a near-black field. The left and right edges dissolve into the background.
behaviour: The row of logos glides steadily in one direction and loops without a visible gap; there is no pause control. Edge gradients dim each icon as it reaches either side.
demo_content: White logo marks for Apple, Google, Facebook, OpenAI and X.
use_when: You want a steady strip of client or partner logos to signal trust without taking much height.
avoid_when: Only five hardcoded brands are included, and a moving strip is slower to scan than a static grid.
customise: Replace the local logos array to choose which brands appear; each entry needs a name for the alt text and an image URL. Gap and fade colours are class name settings.
weight_why: Five repeated logo images on one CSS-animated strip.

a11y.note: The strip never stops and ignores prefers-reduced-motion; each logo does carry alt text.

issues: Logos load from remote SVG URLs, so the strip shows gaps if those hosts are blocked.
The strip cannot be paused, so a visitor cannot hold a logo still to read it.
polish_why: Even spacing and clean fades; the plain icon row and permanent motion keep it standard.
title: Logos Marquee
